name: Kapingamarangi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Elbert, S. (1946). Kapingamarangi and Nukuoro Word List, With Notes on Linguistic Position, Pronunciation, and Grammar. US Military Government.

sources.note: Kapingamarangi (kpg) occurs only in the ISO-639-3 code table; there is no StressTyp2 lect entry for it.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic Languages. Richmond: Curzon.
sources.note: No Kapingamarangi sketch; Kapingamarangi appears only in the classification (Ellicean Outlier / Northwestern Outlier) and the typological-overview source table ('Kapingamarangi [Lieber 1974]'). Stress is discussed only for Oceanic in general ('Stress is generally fully predictable, falling on the penultimate syllable of a word', ch. 3, and POc penultimate stress, §3.1.4); no language-specific statement.

sources.citation: WALS Online, language page 'Kapingamarangi' (wals_code_kpn; source Lieber & Dikepa 1974)
sources.note: No values for features 14A–17A (stress/rhythm chapters); the only source listed is Lieber & Dikepa 1974.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Mentions Kapingamarangi only for syncope of 'unstressed vowels... between identical consonants, giving rise to surface aspirates' (citing Milner 1958) and CV-reduplication with syncope (ppiki, ttuki, llaka); no statement of stress placement.

sources.citation: Goetzfridt, Nicholas J. & Mark C. Goniwiecha. 1989. Language Dictionaries and Grammars of Guam and Micronesia. ERIC ED389163, 43 pp. (annotated bibliography)
sources.note: Nothing; its Kapingamarangi section (p. 19) lists only Lieber & Dikepa 1974 and notes that 'three appendices detail linguistic fine points'.

sources.citation: Lieber, Michael D. & Kalio H. Dikepa. 1974. Kapingamarangi Lexicon. PALI Language Texts: Polynesia. Honolulu: University Press of Hawaii. Open Access edition 2019 (PDF ISBN 9780824881320), 1044 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Intro §2 'The Kapingamarangi Orthography' (pp. xviii–xxi) covers only short/long vowels (10 vowels) and short/long consonants (18 consonants); §7 stem morphology describes reduplication by syllable shape (V/CV vs VV/CVV) without reference to stress; Appendix 1 'Phonetic Description of Kapingamarangi Orthographic Symbols' (pp. 971–972) lists segment articulations and vowel length only. Whole-text search for stress/accent/prominence/loud/emphatic yields no suprasegmental statement (only 'ancestress', 'speak loudly', 'EMPHATIC FORM' of pronouns).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kapingamarangi language' (phonology section derived from Lieber & Dikepa 1974: xvi–xvii and Elbert 1946)
sources.note: Consonants (18, plain vs aspirated/long), 10 vowels, diphthongs, syllable shapes VV/VVV/VCV/CVV/CCVV/CVCV/CCVCV; no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Elbert, Samuel H. 1948. Grammar and comparative study of the language of Kapingamarangi, texts, and word lists. Mimeographed final report to the Pacific Science Board, National Research Council (CIMA), 289 pp. (Glottolog: Elbert 1950, grammar_sketch)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only grammar of the language in Glottolog's descriptive bibliography; a 289-page grammar with texts is the most likely place for an explicit stress statement, and it is the direct predecessor of Lieber & Dikepa's orthography.

sources.citation: Krupa, Viktor. 1982. The Polynesian Languages: A Guide. London: Routledge & Kegan Paul.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Family-wide survey with a phonology chapter that reports stress for individual Polynesian languages including Outliers; could give a second-hand statement for Kapingamarangi citing Elbert 1948.

sources.citation: Carroll, Vern & Tobias Soulik. 1973. Nukuoro Lexicon. PALI Language Texts: Polynesia. Honolulu: University Press of Hawaii.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Lieber & Dikepa adopted this work's orthography 'with several modifications to suit the Kapinga pronunciation'; if its introduction states stress for Nukuoro (nuku1260, the sister Northwestern-Outlier language) it would indicate what the Kapingamarangi authors took for granted — but it is not a Kapingamarangi description.

sources.citation: Emory, Kenneth P. 1965. Kapingamarangi: social and religious life of a Polynesian atoll. Bernice P. Bishop Museum Bulletin 228. Honolulu: Bishop Museum Press, 358 pp.

sources.note: Ethnography by Elbert's 1947 co-fieldworker; Bishop Museum bulletins of this era often carry a language/orthography note that could state stress. Not digitized on the Bishop Museum bulletins page.
